cars.generation: Original CT4-V Blackwing production-road compact-performance family

cars.generation: Fourth-generation Megane Renault Sport production-road hatchback family
cars.variant: R.S. Trophy-R 300 — September 2019 Swiss factory reference
cars.specification_market: Renault Suisse Italian-language brochure printed September 2019: pages 11, 15 and 20. Read the Trophy-R 300 table, not page 23’s ordinary R.S./Trophy descriptions. Optional carbon wheels and 390-mm carbon-ceramic package are not standard; 4CONTROL is not transferred. The hood material translation is ambiguous and omitted. Weight reduction and lap times are not universal configuration claims. One fourth-generation family is counted.
cars.summary: The fourth-generation Megane Trophy-R carries Renault Sport’s focused hot-hatch tradition into a five-door, two-seat road car. Its rear-seat deletion, lighter rear axle, manual gearbox and Torsen differential make this a substantive lightweight performance programme, distinct from the archived second- and third-generation cars.

cars.generation: Second modern MINI R56 production-road hatchback generation
cars.variant: John Cooper Works GP — 2012 global factory announcement reference
cars.specification_market: Global factory press kit dated 9 November 2012 describes 2012 presentation/production; 2012 denotes this reference, not an inferred US 2013 model year. Standard torque is 260 Nm; 280 Nm is temporary overboost. EDLC is brake-based control, not a mechanical limited-slip differential. Optional alternative tyres and track lap claims are omitted. Existing first modern R53 Cooper S remains one record; no separate R53 GP is added.
cars.summary: The R56 John Cooper Works GP turns the second modern MINI generation into a focused two-seat road hatch with adjustable coilovers and substantial racing-derived brakes. Its dedicated chassis and aerodynamic development make it an exceptional hot-hatch reference, beyond a cosmetic package of the archived R53 Cooper S.
cars.admission_reason: The R56 John Cooper Works GP turns the second modern MINI generation into a focused two-seat road hatch with adjustable coilovers and substantial racing-derived brakes. cars.generation: Third modern MINI F56 production-road hatchback generation
cars.variant: John Cooper Works GP — March 2020 European introduction
cars.specification_market: Original German 20 November 2019 release specifies March 2020 deliveries. Select its European tune and automatic, not a manual, GP concept, later GP Pack or additional body. No production total, test-development lap claim or prior-generation historical engine description is imported. The 2012 and 2020 GP references represent absent R56/F56 generations; they do not add two grades to one generation.
cars.summary: The F56 John Cooper Works GP takes the third modern MINI generation to a markedly more powerful two-seat road specification. Its mechanical front differential lock, dedicated chassis and extensive engine/cooling development make it an exceptional performance hatch, with substantive engineering beyond cosmetic GP styling.
